title: Quest
description: A quest with a derived status. availableWhen makes it offerable; closedWhen locks it off (decision impact); stages track progress; outcomes are named end-states with effects.

startsAvailable.description: true = available from game start (covers 'always at least one quest open'). If true, availableWhen is ignored.

availableWhen.description: Condition that moves this quest from unknown -> available. Omit + startsAvailable=true for opening quests.

closedWhen.description: Condition that permanently closes this quest off (decision impact).

order.description: intended sequence index; validator checks ordering sanity

description.description: RETROSPECTIVE line — what the protagonist did, shown in the journal once this stage is complete. Not a to-do; the forward-looking routes for the current stage are 'objectives'.

objectives.description: Routes the protagonist could take while this stage is current, in authoring order (the journal renders them in this order). DISPLAY-ONLY: no effects, no goto, no per-objective completion — completeWhen alone decides when the stage is done.

id.description: Stable, unique within this stage. Validator and diff only — never rendered.

text.description: Protagonist-voice INTENTION line — what the protagonist has decided to do, shown while this stage is current.

showIf.description: Visibility gate; omit for always visible. Gates on knowledge and acquaintance — an objective shows only if the protagonist could actually name that route.

outcomes.description: Named end-states (succeeded, failed, refused, ...). Each fires effects.

tags.description: Journal grouping and prioritisation (main vs. side, act, faction) is driven from here — main-vs-side is a tag, never a boolean. If the project declares quest.tagVocabulary in rules.json, tags are linted against it and an off-vocabulary tag is a warning; with no declared vocabulary, any tag is accepted.

journalName.description: Player-facing quest title shown in the journal. Falls back to 'name' when absent — 'name' stays the authoring-facing label.
